narrative_purpose: Corrects the popular picture of one continuous underground internet by contrasting an ideal seamless web with what wild forest mapping actually finds: short-lived local fungal individuals, breaks, regrowth, and overlapping patches.
subject: A matched underground forest cutaway shown in two halves. Left: every tree root is joined by one continuous, evenly glowing fungal lattice stretching without interruption across the entire soil volume. Right: the same number of trees stand above a mosaic of separate fungal patches; some threads link two or three roots, others end abruptly at gaps, one broken strand is regrowing around a stone, and several patches overlap without merging into one body.
scene: Two versions of the same forest floor, idealized continuity beside the transient patchwork observed in wild ground.
camera: Straight-on side cutaway at matched scale, showing tree bases above and the complete soil volume below.
light: The ideal web glows evenly and continuously; the wild side glows in irregular local islands with dark breaks between them.
palette: Cool soil and root tones, continuous cyan on the ideal side, varied dim teal-cyan patches on the wild side.
style: Painterly forest-soil naturalist plate with enough schematic clarity to compare connectivity.
detail_level: Fine hyphae and broken tips crisp in the foreground; deeper soil dissolves softly.
composition: Equal left and right soil panels separated by a dark vertical gutter, with open dark margins for callouts.
exclude: perfect symmetry on the wild side
consistency_notes: Both halves must contain the same trees. The only changed variable is network continuity: seamless single web versus irregular temporary local patches.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no labels, no arrows, no vector infographic, no photographic or glossy 3D look, no perfectly uniform fungal grid
